text:
alex: Heads-up — while testing quick-switch I saw an insights panel populate with rows from the previously selected org. looks like the prefetch heuristic is not binding tenant context consistently.

maria: ugh. can you repro reliably? :eyes:

alex: yes repro steps: 1) open org A dashboard, 2) quick-switch to org B via header dropdown, 3) open Insights -> Panel X, sometimes you briefly see org A rows then they get replaced. race window ~200-400ms.

priya: do we have traces? which service is responsible for prefetching?

alex: gateway does a prefetch call to /internal/insights/prefetch with header `x-tenant-scope`. then console calls the adapter which hits the runlist service. suspect header gets dropped in fast-path routing.

sam: any logs? can you paste the raw request/response?

alex: pasted snippets: ```
Request: GET /internal/insights/prefetch
Headers: x-tenant-scope: org-b (expected)
Body: { panel_id: "X", filters: {...} }
Response: 200, rows: [ {tenant: "org-a", id: 123, ...}, ... ]
```

maria: that implies downstream cached response keyed incorrectly. maybe the cache key excludes tenant header for small payloads.

priya: also possible: routing heuristic routes to a warm instance that still had previous ctx in in-memory prefetch map. we recently changed affinity to prefer low-latency node which reuses per-instance KV.

sam: @devops-bot can you check if any canary rollout touched the gateway prefetch path in last 24h?

devops-bot: Canary rollout 2026-03-20T11:02:00 completed for service `console-gateway` revision v2.14.3 (changeset: remove-latency-favoring-affinity). No other changes detected.

alex: that aligns with when we first saw user reports. PR attached: github.com/redwood/console/pull/3221

priya: quick hypothesis: we moved affinity to reuse containers and added a cheap in-memory prefetch cache with TTL 5s. cache key uses panel+filters but omitted tenant. fix is to include `tenant_id` and add assertion in router.

maria: agree. also we should add tracing annotation so we can see tenant flow in traces — right now traces show request IDs but not tenant.

sam: low-risk patch: include tenant in cache key + make prefetch cache sharding per-tenant. I can drop a hotfix if you want.

alex: +1. also add an invariant check in internal API: if `x-tenant-scope` header present and row.tenant != header -> log and tag 4xx metric. throw in dev for unit tests.

priya: add integration test that does rapid quickswitch to catch race by firing 50 toggles in 1s and assert no cross-tenant rows.

maria: for rollout: canary to 5% with telemetry guard: if we see >0.01% tenant mismatch errors, rollback.

sam: I'll open a hotfix branch now. pinging @sre-oncall to coordinate metrics and alert.

sre-oncall: got it, creating a temporary metric `console.prefetch.tenant_mismatch` and a grafana panel. will alert Slack if rate > 1/min at 5% traffic.

alex: PR for patch: github.com/redwood/console/pull/3223 — includes cache key change, router assertion, and a small trace tag `tenant_id`.

maria: LGTM but please add changelog note and a migration comment in code for future.

priya: also suggest adding a lint rule that warns when internal caches are created without a tenant scoping argument. we've seen this pattern before.

sam: good call. I'll add a codeowner review from eng-platform and eng-runtime.

alex: repro and basic tests pass locally. will deploy hotfix to canary in 10min.

devops-bot: Deploy started: console-gateway v2.14.4-hotfix -> canary-5%

sre-oncall: metrics panel up, will watch for tenant_mismatch spikes.

maria: if canary looks good for 30m, roll to 50% then full.

alex: after patch we should audit other caches (insights, runlist, runlist-queue) for missing tenant keys. i can make a grep rule to find cache constructors missing `tenant` arg.

priya: let's add that audit to the patch checklist.

sam: noted. thanks everyone. :+1:

maria: leaving this thread open for post-deploy notes. if we get anything funky, paste logs here.

alex: thanks — will update in ~30m with canary results.
